clue.text: Football team depressed about very best wingers being missing

indicators.note: about here means turned round, so the synonym for depressed is read backwards

parts.note: depressed means low, feeling down

indicators.note: the wingers of a word are its outer letters, and with them missing only the inside is kept

explanation.surface: A football side, playing badly, has lost its star wide players.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' turns LOW to WOL; 'wingers being missing' strips B and T from best, leaving ES. WOLVES is the nickname of Wolverhampton Wanderers, an English football club.
explanation.definitionFit: Wolves is the familiar nickname of Wolverhampton Wanderers, an English football club, so it names a team.

clue.text: Like event at rink that's postponed

definitions.meaning: a show performed on a frozen skating surface takes place on the frozen sheet
a plan put aside for later is said to be held in cold storage, idiomatically

explanation.definitionFit: An ice show happens on the frozen surface, and a deferred plan is idiomatically kept in cold storage.

clue.text: Forcefulness of macho types in very English part of the Establishment

indicators.note: in here puts the macho types inside the other pieces, between English and the church

parts.note: CE is the Church of England, part of the British Establishment
he-men are tough, macho types

explanation.surface: Tough guys within the English Establishment are said to show great forcefulness.
explanation.walkthrough: The Church of England (CE) counts as part of the Establishment, the traditional ruling institutions of Britain.
explanation.definitionFit: Vehemence is strong passion or intensity of feeling, a close synonym of forcefulness.

clue.text: Beetle brings endless alarm to sailor

indicators.note: endless means the last letter of the word for alarm is dropped

parts.note: a scare is a sudden alarm
AB, able-bodied seaman, is the usual crossword sailor

explanation.surface: An insect gives a seaman an endless fright.
explanation.definitionFit: A scarab is a dung beetle, sacred in ancient Egypt, so it is a kind of beetle.

clue.text: Game in naval station followed by dance

indicators.note: followed by means the dance comes after the naval station in the answer

parts.note: a naval base is a station for ships
a ball is a formal dance

explanation.surface: Sailors at a naval base play a sport and then hold a dance.
explanation.definitionFit: Baseball is a bat-and-ball sport, an example of a game.

clue.text: Food dished out in US banquets — truth!

indicators.note: dished out suggests food being served up messily, signalling the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone serves a vegetable at American feasts and insists it's the truth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dished out' rearranges the fifteen letters of US BANQUETS TRUTH.
explanation.definitionFit: Butternut squash is a vegetable eaten as food, a winter gourd with orange flesh.

clue.text: Dismissed from uni with less of an odour, we hear?

indicators.note: we hear signals that the phrase is spoken and the spelling changed

parts.note: a smell turned down is a scent reduced, so this is scent down

explanation.surface: A student expelled from university might, in jest, smell less.
explanation.walkthrough: 'we hear' turns SCENT DOWN (a smell lowered) into a phrase that sounds the same. In Britain, a student expelled from university is said to be sent down.
explanation.definitionFit: Being sent down is the British term for expulsion from university, especially Oxford or Cambridge.

clue.text: Part of body has nasty smell, not totally healthy

parts.note: BO is body odour, a nasty smell

indicators.note: not totally means the last letter of the word for healthy is cut off

parts.note: well means in good health

explanation.surface: A patient's body part smells foul and they are not quite healthy.
explanation.definitionFit: The bowel is the intestine, an internal organ and so a part of the body.

clue.text: Being illuminated, he tingled with excitement

indicators.note: with excitement suggests letters jumping about, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: A man tingled with excitement as the light fell on him.
explanation.definitionFit: Lightened can mean made brighter or lit up, matching being illuminated.

clue.text: Dismay is hidden by adherent being put out

indicators.note: hidden by means is is placed inside the other piece
put out suggests disarray, so the letters of adherent are rearranged

explanation.surface: A loyal follower is upset, and dismay is concealed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hidden by' looks like a hidden-word signal, but here it only means IS sits inside the rearranged letters (DHEARTEN) that 'being put out' makes.
explanation.definitionFit: To dishearten is to discourage or dismay someone, a verb synonym.

clue.text: What's earned is money taken to bookie? Not right!

indicators.note: not right means the letter for right is removed

parts.note: a wager is a bet, money taken to a bookmaker

explanation.surface: Someone takes their earnings to the bookie, which isn't wise.
explanation.walkthrough: R is the usual abbreviation for right.
explanation.definitionFit: A wage is the pay earned for work, so it is what's earned.

clue.text: Fellow in dressing-room can be awfully tame in different ways

indicators.note: awfully signals the letters are scrambled
in different ways means the word tame is used twice, each time rearranged differently

explanation.surface: A colleague in the changing room can be strangely tame in various respects.
explanation.walkthrough: TAME is rearranged two different ways, TEAM and MATE, which together form the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A teammate is a fellow player on a side, someone who shares the dressing-room.

clue.text: Expand time for event to accommodate the Italian

indicators.note: to accommodate means one piece holds the other inside

parts.note: a date is the time fixed for an event
il is Italian for the

explanation.surface: Push back the event date to make room for the Italian visitor.
explanation.definitionFit: To dilate is to widen or expand, as pupils do in the dark.

clue.text: Indication of happiness with bother finally swamped by drink

indicators.note: swamped by means the letter is engulfed inside the drink

parts.note: gin is a spirit, a drink

indicators.note: finally picks out the last letter of bother

explanation.surface: Happiness shows when the bother ends in a sea of drink.
explanation.definitionFit: A grin is a broad smile, an outward sign of happiness.

clue.text: Unoriginal girl said to be after money

indicators.note: after means the girl's piece comes after the money

parts.note: the ready is slang for cash

indicators.note: said signals the word for girl is spoken and spelt differently

parts.note: a maid is a girl, an old word for a young woman

explanation.surface: A young woman is reported to be chasing money.
explanation.walkthrough: 'said' gives MADE, which sounds like MAID. 'Ready' or 'readies' is British slang for cash.
explanation.definitionFit: Ready-made means produced in advance, off the peg, hence unoriginal or second-hand in thought.

clue.text: Scientist's going around western communities established quite recently

indicators.note: going around means the scientist's word encloses the other letter

parts.note: Isaac Newton, the physicist; with the possessive, Newton's

explanation.surface: A scientist travels round settlements in the west that were founded recently.
explanation.walkthrough: New towns are British towns planned and built after the Second World War, such as Milton Keynes.
explanation.definitionFit: New towns were planned communities built from scratch in postwar Britain, so established quite recently.

clue.text: Defeat in game at the end of bowler's short spell?

indicators.note: at the end of means the game comes after the bowler's spell

parts.note: in cricket an over is a short spell of six balls by one bowler
a match is a game

explanation.surface: A cricket bowler finishes a brief spell and the match is lost.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket, an OVER is a set of six balls bowled by one bowler.
explanation.definitionFit: To overmatch is to be more than a match for, hence to defeat or outclass.

clue.text: It's not hard to detect an affectionate feeling

parts.note: something not hard is soft
to spot is to detect or notice

explanation.surface: It's easy to tell when someone has tender feelings.
explanation.definitionFit: A soft spot is a fondness or affection for someone, an idiom.

clue.text: Murders escorts

definitions.meaning: to murder is to kill, slang to eliminate
to escort someone is to take them on a date

explanation.definitionFit: Taking someone out can mean killing them or accompanying them on a date, two idioms.

clue.text: Christian Scientist in a whirl

definitions.meaning: Mary Baker, founder of Christian Science
a swirl of water or air

explanation.definitionFit: Mary Baker Eddy founded Christian Science, and a circular current of water is called by the same word.

clue.text: Approval shown by number clutching King James Bible

indicators.note: clutching means the number holds the other piece inside

parts.note: four is a number
AV is the Authorised Version, the King James Bible

explanation.surface: Approval is shown by a group of people holding the King James Bible.
explanation.definitionFit: Favour means approval or support, as in looking on something with favour.

clue.text: Try twisting worker, as terrible boss?

indicators.note: twisting means the letters of try are rearranged

parts.note: an ant is the classic worker in crosswords

explanation.surface: A terrible boss tries to twist a worker's arm.
explanation.definitionFit: A tyrant is a cruel, oppressive ruler, so a terrible boss.

clue.text: A theologian in an elevated position to be convincing

parts.note: DD is Doctor of Divinity, a theologian
up means raised high

explanation.surface: A theologian standing in the pulpit has to be persuasive.
explanation.definitionFit: If an argument adds up, it makes sense and is convincing, an idiom.

clue.text: Mess created by amount of paper spread across annual meeting

indicators.note: spread across means the paper encloses the meeting

parts.note: a quire is 24 or 25 sheets of paper
AGM is an annual general meeting

explanation.surface: Paperwork spread across a company's annual meeting creates chaos.
explanation.definitionFit: A quagmire is boggy ground, figuratively a mess or predicament.

clue.text: Brushes not initially provided for apartments

indicators.note: not initially means the first letter of the word for brushes is missing

parts.note: brooms are brushes for sweeping

explanation.surface: Flats were provided without brooms.
explanation.definitionFit: Rooms can mean lodgings or a set of rooms, i.e. apartments.

clue.text: Told son to get help

parts.note: aid is help

explanation.surface: A son was told to get help.
explanation.definitionFit: Said means spoke or told, a past tense synonym.

clue.text: Seat in front of lots of flats etc.

definitions.text: Seat in front of lots of flats etc.

parts.words: Seat in front of lots of flats etc.
parts.note: flats here are musical notes on black keys, not apartments, so the seat sits before a keyboard

explanation.surface: A seat outside a block of flats.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flats' wants to mean apartments; it means the flat notes on a keyboard, which with sharps and naturals ('etc.') face the player.
explanation.definitionFit: The stool a pianist sits on faces the keys, which include flats and sharps.

clue.text: Dismissal of some French companion when Irishman's brought in

parts.note: des is French for some
Pat is a stereotypical Irishman's name
CH is Companion of Honour

explanation.surface: Some French companion is dismissed when an Irishman arrives.
explanation.definitionFit: Despatch is sending off, hence dismissal.

clue.text: Perhaps an old clue slightly amended about drug

definitions.text: Perhaps an old clue slightly amended

parts.note: re means about, concerning
hash is hashish, a drug

explanation.surface: An old clue reworked by the setter is about drugs.
explanation.definitionFit: A rehash is old material reused with small changes, and a reused clue is an example.
